L.audio_profile: A cheerful woman of 25 with a bright, warm, quick voice; standing outside an arena on a cold winter evening, pleased with herself and trusting, speaking up a little over the far crowd; natural and unpolished, like a friend filming a vlog.

T.audio_profile: A tall, calm man of 30 with a low, dry, casual voice; slow, patient, deadpan and quietly certain; he never raises his voice.

dialogue_turns.text: [bright, thrilled, to the camera, showing it off] Good news! Ice hockey tickets!
[pleased, then reading the name off her phone with great respect] A man sent me a link. Official Dave.
[repeating it slowly, dead flat] Official Dave.
[turning to him, amazed that he has to ask] It's in his name!
[calm and patient, a plain fact] The planner checks ticket links. Paste it.
[quick and defensive, cut off] You never trust any—
[cutting in over her, calm and firm] Paste.
[reading it off her phone, small and quiet] Could not verify.
[reading a new message, smaller still] He says hurry.
[softly, to her phone, fond] Bye, Dave.

payload.scene: A phone vlog on the wide paved forecourt of a big indoor ice hockey arena at blue winter dusk, before the game; cold air, a far muffled crowd drifting toward the lit doors. Luna holds the phone at arm's length and talks to it, her own other phone held up in her free hand like a trophy; Timo stands upright just behind her.
payload.sample_context: A twenty-second comedy sketch played by two close friends who bicker. It must sound like two real people talking, quick and natural, never like an advert or a narrator. LUNA, about 25, is cheerful, quick and trusting; she is thrilled with the tickets a stranger sent her a link for, and she says the stranger's name, Official Dave, with real respect; when the link check comes back she goes small and quiet, and in the end she is fond and a little sad. TIMO, about 30, is slow, dry and proud; he never raises his voice; today he is calm, patient and quietly certain, and he never says I told you so. They answer each other fast, with no gaps between the lines.

text: Good news! Ice hockey tickets! From where? A man sent me a link. Official Dave. Official Dave! It's in his name! The planner checks ticket links. Paste it. You never trust any... Paste! Could not verify. He says, "Hurry!" Bye, Dave.
